lineageUi.languageInfo:
A language you know is one you can speak, read and write. It decides who your character can talk to without help, and it comes up more than new players expect: half the trouble in a dungeon is written on a wall.

Common is the trade tongue everyone shares. The rest are the tongues of particular peoples: Dwarvish, Elvish, Orc, Draconic and so on. Pick whatever fits where your character grew up, or whoever you expect to be negotiating with.

gameHelp.ability_score.short: One of six numbers describing what your character is naturally good at.
gameHelp.ability_score.long: The six are Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma. Most scores land between 8 and 18 at first level. What actually gets added to your rolls is the modifier derived from the score: 10 or 11 gives +0, every 2 points above that adds +1, every 2 below subtracts 1.
gameHelp.modifier.short: The bonus or penalty an ability score adds to your rolls.
gameHelp.modifier.long: Work it out by subtracting 10 from the score and halving the result, rounding down. A score of 16 gives +3, a score of 8 gives -1. You will see modifiers written with a sign, like +3, everywhere on your sheet.
gameHelp.str.short: Raw physical power: hitting things with heavy weapons, shoving, climbing, lifting.
gameHelp.str.long: Most melee weapons use Strength for their attack and damage rolls. It also covers the Athletics skill, and the saving throw against being pushed or restrained.
gameHelp.dex.short: Agility and precision: light weapons, bows, armor class, dodging.
gameHelp.dex.long: Dexterity adds to your armor class in light and medium armor, decides your initiative, and powers finesse and ranged weapons. Its saving throw is the one you make to dodge fireballs and traps.
gameHelp.con.short: Toughness and stamina. It raises your hit points at every level.
gameHelp.con.long: You never roll a Constitution check, but its saving throw comes up constantly: resisting poison, surviving exhaustion, and holding concentration on a spell when you take damage.
gameHelp.int.short: Reasoning and recall. The casting ability for wizards.
gameHelp.int.long: It covers Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature and Religion. Its saving throw resists illusions and effects that attack the mind directly.
gameHelp.wis.short: Perceptiveness and judgement. The casting ability for clerics, druids and rangers.
gameHelp.wis.long: It covers Perception, Insight, Medicine, Survival and Animal Handling, and sets your passive Perception. Its saving throw resists charms, fear and mind control, which makes it one of the most valuable saves in the game.
gameHelp.cha.short: Force of personality. The casting ability for bards, sorcerers, warlocks and paladins.
gameHelp.cha.long: It covers Persuasion, Deception, Intimidation and Performance. Its saving throw resists banishment and possession.
gameHelp.armor_class.short: How hard you are to hit. An attacker must roll this number or higher to land a hit.
gameHelp.armor_class.long: Your AC comes from your armor, your shield, your Dexterity, and any magic or class feature that adds to it. The app works it out for you from what you are wearing. Higher is better, and most characters sit between 12 and 20.
gameHelp.hit_points.short: How much damage you can take before you drop.
gameHelp.hit_points.long: At 0 hit points you fall unconscious and start making death saving throws. Healing brings you back. Your maximum grows every level, based on your class's hit die and your Constitution modifier.
gameHelp.temp_hp.short: A buffer that soaks damage before your real hit points do.
gameHelp.temp_hp.long: They are not healing and do not stack: a new source replaces the old one rather than adding to it. They vanish on a long rest, and any left over when the effect ends are simply lost.
gameHelp.hit_dice.short: A pool of dice you spend during a short rest to heal yourself.
gameHelp.hit_dice.long: You have one per character level, of the size your class uses. Spend one on a short rest to roll it and regain that many hit points plus your Constitution modifier. You get half of them back on a long rest, so they are a resource to ration across a day of adventuring.
gameHelp.ability_check.short: A d20 roll plus a modifier, made when the outcome of something is uncertain.
gameHelp.ability_check.long: The DM sets a difficulty number and you try to meet or beat it. Climbing a wall is a Strength check, spotting an ambush is a Wisdom check. If you are proficient in a relevant skill you add your proficiency bonus too.
gameHelp.saving_throw.short: A d20 roll to resist something happening to you, rather than to make something happen.
gameHelp.saving_throw.long: A dragon breathes fire and you make a Dexterity save to take half damage. A vampire tries to charm you and you make a Wisdom save to shrug it off. Each class is proficient in two of the six saves, adding its proficiency bonus to those.
gameHelp.proficiency_bonus.short: A bonus you add to anything you are trained in. It grows from +2 to +6 as you level.
gameHelp.proficiency_bonus.long: It applies to attacks with weapons you are proficient with, skills you are proficient in, your two saving throw proficiencies, and your spell save DC. It is +2 at levels 1 to 4 and rises by 1 every four levels after that.
gameHelp.advantage.short: Roll two d20s and keep the higher one.
gameHelp.advantage.long: You get it when circumstances favour you: attacking an unaware enemy, or acting on information an ally gave you. Advantage and disadvantage cancel out exactly, no matter how many sources of each you have, and they never stack with themselves.
gameHelp.disadvantage.short: Roll two d20s and keep the lower one.
gameHelp.disadvantage.long: You get it when circumstances work against you: attacking at long range, fighting blind, or acting while poisoned or frightened. It cancels out with advantage exactly.
gameHelp.initiative.short: A Dexterity roll at the start of a fight that sets the turn order.
gameHelp.initiative.long: Everyone rolls once, and the round then runs from highest to lowest. The order holds until the fight ends.
gameHelp.action.short: The main thing you do on your turn: attack, cast a spell, dash, hide, help an ally.
gameHelp.action.long: Each turn you get one action, one bonus action, your movement, and one reaction that you can use before your next turn. Most turns are an action plus movement; bonus actions only exist when a feature or spell specifically grants one.
gameHelp.bonus_action.short: A quick extra thing on your turn, but only when something specifically grants one.
gameHelp.bonus_action.long: You cannot invent a bonus action: a class feature, a spell or a weapon has to say it uses one. You get at most one per turn, so features that compete for it force a real choice.
gameHelp.reaction.short: One response you can make between your turns, triggered by something specific.
gameHelp.reaction.long: The most common one is an opportunity attack when an enemy walks out of your reach. Spells like shield and features like Uncanny Dodge also use it. You get one and it comes back at the start of your turn.
gameHelp.attack_roll.short: A d20 plus your ability modifier and proficiency bonus, against the target's AC.
gameHelp.attack_roll.long: Meet or beat the AC and you hit, then roll the weapon or spell's damage. A natural 20 always hits and doubles the damage dice, and a natural 1 always misses.
gameHelp.critical_hit.short: A natural 20 on an attack roll. You roll all the damage dice twice.
gameHelp.critical_hit.long: Only the dice double, not the flat modifiers. Some features widen the range so a 19 counts too.
gameHelp.spell_slot.short: The fuel for casting a spell. You have a limited number of each level per day.
gameHelp.spell_slot.long: Casting a 1st-level spell spends a 1st-level slot or higher. Casting a spell with a bigger slot than it needs often makes it stronger, which is called upcasting. Most casters get their slots back on a long rest; warlocks get theirs back on a short one.
gameHelp.cantrip.short: A level 0 spell you can cast as often as you like, with no slot.
gameHelp.cantrip.long: Cantrips get stronger on their own at character levels 5, 11 and 17, which is why an attack cantrip stays useful all game.
gameHelp.spell_save_dc.short: The number an enemy must beat to resist your spell.
gameHelp.spell_save_dc.long: It is 8 plus your proficiency bonus plus your spellcasting ability modifier. The app calculates it for you and shows it on your sheet.
gameHelp.concentration.short: Some spells only last while you keep concentrating, and you can only concentrate on one at a time.
gameHelp.concentration.long: Casting a second concentration spell ends the first. Taking damage forces a Constitution saving throw against 10 or half the damage, whichever is higher, and failing it ends the spell. Being knocked unconscious ends it too.
gameHelp.ritual.short: A spell you can cast without spending a slot by taking 10 extra minutes over it.
gameHelp.ritual.long: Only spells marked as rituals can be cast this way, and only if your class supports ritual casting. It is free but far too slow for combat.
gameHelp.prepared_spells.short: Which spells you actually have available today.
gameHelp.prepared_spells.long: Some classes know a fixed short list forever, like bards and sorcerers. Others, like clerics and wizards, choose a fresh set after each long rest from a much bigger pool. Either way you can only cast what is on the list, and only while you have slots left.
gameHelp.short_rest.short: About an hour of downtime. You can spend Hit Dice to heal and recover some abilities.
gameHelp.short_rest.long: Features that say short rest come back, including warlock spell slots, monk ki, and a fighter's Second Wind and Action Surge. You can take several in a day.
gameHelp.long_rest.short: About eight hours of sleep. You regain all hit points and almost everything else.
gameHelp.long_rest.long: You get all your spell slots and long-rest features back and half your spent Hit Dice. You only benefit from one per 24 hours.
gameHelp.death_save.short: At 0 hit points you roll a d20 each turn to see whether you stabilize or die.
gameHelp.death_save.long: 10 or higher is a success, under 10 is a failure. Three successes and you stabilize; three failures and you die. A natural 20 puts you back up at 1 hit point, a natural 1 counts as two failures, and any healing at all wakes you immediately.
gameHelp.condition.short: A status effect that changes what you can do, like poisoned, frightened or stunned.
gameHelp.condition.long: Most conditions let you repeat a saving throw at the end of your turns to shake them off. The app tracks the ones you have and applies their effects to your rolls automatically.
gameHelp.exhaustion.short: A stacking penalty from six levels of increasing severity. Level 6 is death.
gameHelp.exhaustion.long: It comes from forced marches, going without sleep, and a few powerful abilities that trade stamina for effect. A long rest with food and drink removes one level.
gameHelp.attunement.short: A bond with a magic item, formed over a short rest. You can hold three at once.
gameHelp.attunement.long: Items that require attunement do nothing until you attune to them, so the three-slot limit is a real choice about which magic you carry.
gameHelp.difficult_terrain.short: Ground that costs double movement: rubble, deep snow, undergrowth, a crowd.
gameHelp.difficult_terrain.long: Moving 10 feet through it uses 20 feet of your speed. Some features let you ignore it.
gameHelp.cover.short: Something between you and an attacker makes you harder to hit.
gameHelp.cover.long: Half cover gives +2 AC and +2 on Dexterity saves, three-quarters cover gives +5, and total cover means you cannot be targeted directly at all.
gameHelp.opportunity_attack.short: A free swing when an enemy walks out of your reach.
gameHelp.opportunity_attack.long: It uses your reaction and happens as they leave. Taking the Disengage action avoids provoking it, which is why rogues get Disengage as a bonus action.
gameHelp.passive_perception.short: A standing score for what you notice without looking. 10 plus your Perception bonus.
gameHelp.passive_perception.long: The DM checks it against hidden things so nobody has to keep rolling. A higher passive Perception means traps and ambushes are spotted before they matter.
gameHelp.skill.short: A narrow area of expertise attached to an ability, like Stealth or Persuasion.
gameHelp.skill.long: Being proficient in a skill adds your proficiency bonus to checks that use it. You do not need proficiency to try, only to be reliably good at it.
gameHelp.expertise.short: Doubled proficiency bonus on a chosen skill, so you rarely fail at it.
gameHelp.expertise.long: Rogues and bards get it. On a skill you already have proficiency in, it makes you the party's clear specialist.
gameHelp.level.short: How experienced your character is, from 1 to 20. Higher levels bring more hit points, features and spells.
gameHelp.level.long: Levelling happens between sessions or at a milestone in the story. The app walks you through each choice a new level gives you.
gameHelp.subclass.short: A specialization within your class, chosen at level 1, 2 or 3 depending on the class.
gameHelp.subclass.long: Two fighters can play completely differently based on this one choice: a Battle Master spends dice on tactical maneuvers, an Eldritch Knight casts wizard spells. It is the biggest single decision about how your character plays.
closedHelp.condition.blinded.name: blinded
closedHelp.condition.blinded.blurb: Cannot see. Fails any check that needs sight; attacks against it have advantage, its own attacks have disadvantage.
closedHelp.condition.charmed.name: charmed
closedHelp.condition.charmed.blurb: Cannot attack the charmer or target them with harmful effects; the charmer has advantage on social checks against it.
closedHelp.condition.deafened.name: deafened
closedHelp.condition.deafened.blurb: Cannot hear. Fails any check that needs hearing.
closedHelp.condition.exhaustion.name: exhaustion
closedHelp.condition.exhaustion.blurb: Six worsening levels, from disadvantage on checks to death. Usually one level clears per long rest.
closedHelp.condition.frightened.name: frightened
closedHelp.condition.frightened.blurb: Disadvantage on checks and attacks while the source of fear is in sight, and cannot willingly move closer to it.
closedHelp.condition.grappled.name: grappled
closedHelp.condition.grappled.blurb: Speed becomes 0. Ends if the grappler is incapacitated or the two are forced apart.
closedHelp.condition.incapacitated.name: incapacitated
closedHelp.condition.invisible.name: invisible
closedHelp.condition.invisible.blurb: Cannot be seen without magic or a special sense. Attacks against it have disadvantage, its attacks have advantage.
closedHelp.condition.paralyzed.name: paralyzed
closedHelp.condition.paralyzed.blurb: Incapacitated and cannot move or speak. Auto-fails Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks against it have advantage and hit within 5 feet are critical.
closedHelp.condition.petrified.name: petrified
closedHelp.condition.petrified.blurb: Turned to stone: incapacitated, unaware, weighs ten times as much, resists all damage, immune to poison and disease.
closedHelp.condition.poisoned.name: poisoned
closedHelp.condition.poisoned.blurb: Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.
closedHelp.condition.prone.name: prone
closedHelp.condition.prone.blurb: Must crawl or spend half its movement to stand. Disadvantage on attacks; melee attacks against it have advantage, ranged ones disadvantage.
closedHelp.condition.restrained.name: restrained
closedHelp.condition.restrained.blurb: Speed 0. Attacks against it have advantage, its attacks have disadvantage, and it has disadvantage on Dexterity saves.
closedHelp.condition.stunned.name: stunned
closedHelp.condition.stunned.blurb: Incapacitated, cannot move, speaks falteringly. Auto-fails Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks against it have advantage.
closedHelp.condition.unconscious.name: unconscious
closedHelp.condition.unconscious.blurb: Incapacitated, unaware, drops what it holds and falls prone. Auto-fails Strength and Dexterity saves; attacks have advantage and hit within 5 feet are critical.
closedHelp.school.abjuration.name: abjuration
closedHelp.school.abjuration.blurb: Protection and banishment: wards, shields, dispelling, and sending things back where they came from.
closedHelp.school.conjuration.name: conjuration
closedHelp.school.conjuration.blurb: Bringing things into being or across distance: summoned creatures, conjured objects, teleportation.
closedHelp.school.divination.name: divination
closedHelp.school.divination.blurb: Knowing: seeing far, reading thoughts, finding what is hidden, glimpsing what is to come.
closedHelp.school.enchantment.name: enchantment
closedHelp.school.enchantment.blurb: Influencing minds: charm, fear, sleep, suggestion, and commands the target cannot refuse.
closedHelp.school.evocation.name: evocation
closedHelp.school.evocation.blurb: Raw energy: fire, lightning, cold and force, most of the blasting spells and the healing ones.
closedHelp.school.illusion.name: illusion
closedHelp.school.illusion.blurb: Deceiving the senses: images, sounds, disguises and phantasms that are not really there.
closedHelp.school.necromancy.name: necromancy
closedHelp.school.necromancy.blurb: Life and death: draining vitality, raising the dead, speaking with them, and undoing death.
closedHelp.school.transmutation.name: transmutation
closedHelp.school.transmutation.blurb: Changing what is: shape, size, substance or speed of creatures and things.
closedHelp.property.ammunition.name: ammunition
closedHelp.property.ammunition.blurb: Needs arrows, bolts or stones to attack at range; the ammunition is spent as it is fired.
closedHelp.property.double-headed.name: double-headed
closedHelp.property.double-headed.blurb: A weapon with a striking end at each side; the second end can make the extra light-weapon attack, doing the die in brackets.
closedHelp.property.finesse.name: finesse
closedHelp.property.finesse.blurb: Attack and damage may use Dexterity instead of Strength, whichever is better.
closedHelp.property.gunpowder.name: gunpowder
closedHelp.property.gunpowder.blurb: Fires with black powder, which it consumes along with the shot; wet or missing powder means it cannot fire.
closedHelp.property.heavy.name: heavy
closedHelp.property.heavy.blurb: Too big for Small creatures to use well: they attack with disadvantage.
closedHelp.property.light.name: light
closedHelp.property.light.blurb: Small enough to fight with one in each hand (two-weapon fighting).
closedHelp.property.loading.name: loading
closedHelp.property.loading.blurb: Slow to reload: only one shot per action, bonus action or reaction, however many attacks you have.
closedHelp.property.magazine.name: magazine
closedHelp.property.magazine.blurb: Holds the number of shots in brackets; once they are spent, an action reloads it.
closedHelp.property.reach.name: reach
closedHelp.property.reach.blurb: Strikes 5 feet further than usual, so 10 feet away instead of 5.
closedHelp.property.special.name: special
closedHelp.property.special.blurb: Has its own rules beyond the usual attack; the DM applies them when it is used.
closedHelp.property.thrown.name: thrown
closedHelp.property.thrown.blurb: Can be thrown to make a ranged attack, using the same ability as a melee swing with it.
closedHelp.property.two-handed.name: two-handed
closedHelp.property.two-handed.blurb: Needs both hands to attack with, so no shield or second weapon.
closedHelp.property.versatile.name: versatile
closedHelp.property.versatile.blurb: Usable in one hand or two; the two-handed grip does the larger damage die in brackets.
closedHelp.damage.acid.name: acid
closedHelp.damage.acid.blurb: Corrosive: sprays, oozes and dissolving breath.
closedHelp.damage.bludgeoning.name: bludgeoning
closedHelp.damage.bludgeoning.blurb: Blunt force: clubs, hammers, fists, falling.
closedHelp.damage.cold.name: cold
closedHelp.damage.cold.blurb: Freezing: ice breath, rays of frost, winter magic.
closedHelp.damage.fire.name: fire
closedHelp.damage.force.name: force
closedHelp.damage.force.blurb: Pure magical energy; almost nothing resists it (magic missile, eldritch blast).
closedHelp.damage.lightning.name: lightning
closedHelp.damage.lightning.blurb: Electricity: bolts, blue dragons, storm magic.
closedHelp.damage.necrotic.name: necrotic
closedHelp.damage.necrotic.blurb: Withering life force: undead touches, life drain, most death magic.
closedHelp.damage.piercing.name: piercing
closedHelp.damage.poison.name: poison
closedHelp.damage.poison.blurb: Venom and toxins: stings, poisoned blades, poison breath.
closedHelp.damage.psychic.name: psychic
closedHelp.damage.psychic.blurb: Mental assault: mind flayers, some enchantments, telepathic damage.
closedHelp.damage.radiant.name: radiant
closedHelp.damage.radiant.blurb: Holy light and searing brilliance: celestials, clerics' spells, the sun.
closedHelp.damage.slashing.name: slashing
closedHelp.damage.thunder.name: thunder
closedHelp.damage.thunder.blurb: Concussive sound: thunderwave, shatter, a giant's shout.
closedHelp.size.tiny.name: tiny
closedHelp.size.tiny.blurb: About the size of a cat or smaller; occupies a 2.5 foot square.
closedHelp.size.small.name: small
closedHelp.size.small.blurb: Halfling-sized; fills a 5 foot square but wields heavy weapons badly.
closedHelp.size.medium.name: medium
closedHelp.size.large.name: large
closedHelp.size.large.blurb: Horse or ogre sized; fills a 10 foot square.
closedHelp.size.huge.name: huge
closedHelp.size.huge.blurb: Giant or young dragon sized; fills a 15 foot square.
closedHelp.size.gargantuan.name: gargantuan
closedHelp.size.gargantuan.blurb: Ancient dragons, krakens; 20 feet or more on a side.
callingUi.subclassAdvice: Your {subclass} is the biggest choice about how this character plays. Tap the info icon next to any option to read what it does before choosing.
callingUi.subclassLocked: A {class} chooses a {subclass} at level {unlock}; there is nothing to pick at level {level}. The choice comes with that level-up.
callingUi.gainHelp: Tap any name to read what it does. Racial traits and background perks are added on top when the character is saved.
callingUi.skillsAdvice: A {skill} you are proficient in adds your {proficiency} to rolls that use it. Tap any ⓘ to see which ability a skill leans on. A greyed skill is already yours from your race or background, so a class pick on it would be wasted.
callingUi.owned:
{skill} is already yours: your {source}{by} grants it{trait}, so it is not offered as a class pick here.

{help}
callingUi.expertiseHelp: {expertise} doubles your {proficiency} on the chosen skills.
callingUi.skillsFirst: Pick your class skills above first.
callingUi.thievesHelp: Your proficiency bonus is doubled for ability checks you make with thieves' tools.
callingUi.styleHelp: {count} still to choose. A fighting style is a permanent edge with one kind of weapon or armour; read each card before picking.
callingUi.optionsHelp: These are real abilities your character gets. Tap the info button on any one to read what it does.
callingUi.styleDescription.archery: +2 to attack rolls with ranged weapons.
callingUi.styleDescription.dueling: +2 damage with a one-handed melee weapon and no other weapon in hand.
callingUi.styleDescription.great_weapon_: Reroll 1s and 2s on damage with a two-handed or versatile melee weapon.
callingUi.styleDescription.protection: Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack against an ally within 5 ft, using your shield.
callingUi.styleDescription.two_weapon_fi: Add your ability modifier to the damage of your off-hand attack.
callingMaterial.class.artificer.blurb: An inventor who casts through gadgets and infuses gear with magic, part tinkerer, part battlefield support.
callingMaterial.class.barbarian.blurb: A fierce warrior who rages into battle, shrugging off blows that would fell anyone else.
callingMaterial.class.bard.blurb: A performer whose music and wit are magic, inspiring allies and unsettling foes.
callingMaterial.class.cleric.blurb: A champion of a god, wielding divine magic to heal, protect and smite.
callingMaterial.class.druid.blurb: A keeper of the wild who commands nature's magic and takes the shapes of beasts.
callingMaterial.class.fighter.blurb: A master of arms and armor, the most versatile combatant in any party.
callingMaterial.class.monk.blurb: A disciplined martial artist who channels ki into speed, precision and uncanny feats.
callingMaterial.class.paladin.blurb: A holy warrior bound by an oath, backing steel with divine smites and healing.
callingMaterial.class.ranger.blurb: A hunter and tracker of the wilds, deadly with a bow and at home far from any road.
callingMaterial.class.rogue.blurb: A cunning specialist in stealth, skill and the devastating sneak attack.
callingMaterial.class.sorcerer.blurb: A caster born with magic in the blood, bending raw power with metamagic.
callingMaterial.class.warlock.blurb: A wielder of magic bargained from an otherworldly patron, built around eldritch invocations.
callingMaterial.class.wizard.blurb: A scholar of the arcane who studies spells into a spellbook and prepares them each day.
callingMaterial.class.netrunner.blurb: A console cowboy who cracks systems and minds alike, running intrusion programs from a battered cyberdeck.
callingMaterial.class.street_samurai.blu: Chromed to the teeth and faster than thought, a blade-and-bullet artist who sells violence with a warranty.
callingMaterial.class.rigger.blurb: A drone whisperer who rides camera feeds, jury-rigs machines, and casts support routines through a loyal swarm.
callingMaterial.class.fixer.blurb: The one who knows a guy. Contacts, favors, and a silver tongue open doors that guns cannot.
callingMaterial.class.esper.blurb: A psychic surge burns behind their eyes: raw, unstable psionics that megacorp labs would kill to bottle.
callingMaterial.class.trauma_doc.blurb: Combat medic with a stim gun and a nanite pharmacy, keeping the crew breathing through the firefight.
callingMaterial.class.witch_hunter.blurb: Grim inquisitor with litanies on the lips and silver shot in the gun, hunting the corruption behind pious faces.
callingMaterial.class.plague_doctor.blur: Behind the beaked mask, a mind that reads sickness like scripture and turns remedies into weapons.
callingMaterial.class.grave_knight.blurb: Sworn to a power in the earth, they carry a blade that answers their call and an aura of the tomb.
callingMaterial.class.penitent.blurb: Every scar a prayer. They spend their own blood like coin and grow stronger the closer they walk to death.
callingMaterial.class.dirgesinger.blurb: A voice for the grieving and the graves: songs that mourn, curse, and occasionally raise what should stay down.
callingMaterial.class.vermin_lord.blurb: King of the gutters. The rats scout for them, the sewers are their roads, and nothing in the city moves unseen.
callingMaterial.class.exorcist.blurb: Armed with rites, salt, and stubborn faith, they drive out the things that wear people like coats.
callingMaterial.class.occultist.blurb: A scholar who read the forbidden pages anyway, trading pieces of sleep and sanity for real power.
callingMaterial.class.survivor.blurb: They have outlived everyone who called them lucky. Fast hands, cold nerve, and an exit always in mind.
callingMaterial.class.slayer.blurb: A monster hunter of the old orders: silver on the blade, lore in the head, and no illusions left.
callingMaterial.class.parapsychologist.b: Science aimed at the impossible: field instruments, careful notes, and effects the journals refuse to print.
callingMaterial.class.apostate.blurb: They escaped the cult, but the ritual finished anyway. Now its power lives under their skin.
callingMaterial.class.detective.blurb: Nothing escapes them: a trained eye for detail, a memory like a case file, and a nose for lies.
callingMaterial.class.alienist.blurb: A doctor of the mind whose treatments border on the uncanny: reading motives, unknotting fear, opening memory.
callingMaterial.class.grifter.blurb: Charm as a weapon, a new name in every city, and a plan that is always three lies deep.
callingMaterial.class.enforcer.blurb: The wall between trouble and the people they protect. Big fists, bigger presence, unexpected patience.
callingMaterial.class.muckraker.blurb: A reporter who follows the money, kicks over rocks, and prints what powerful people pay to bury.
callingMaterial.class.spirit_medium.blur: The dead talk to them, whether invited or not. Séances, warnings, and truths the living lie about.
callingMaterial.class.scavenger.blurb: The ruins provide, if you know where to look. Quick fingers, sharp eyes, and a bag of exactly the right junk.
callingMaterial.class.road_warrior.blurb: Chrome-spiked and fearless, living fast on the dead highways where the loudest engine makes the law.
callingMaterial.class.aberrant.blurb: The Fall rewrote them. Mutation is their magic, unstable and blooming, and their body never stopped adapting.
callingMaterial.class.salvage_tech.blurb: They coax old-world machines back to life and wield rebuilt wonders the new world barely understands.
callingMaterial.class.waste_preacher.blu: A voice crying hope in the wasteland. Their sermons close wounds, steady hands, and occasionally call down judgment.
callingMaterial.class.packmaster.blurb: Bonded to the wasteland's beasts, they run with a loyal companion and speak the old green tongue of survival.
callingMaterial.class.machinist.blurb: Engineer-arcanist whose schematics bend aether through brass: spells assembled, not spoken.
callingMaterial.class.aeronaut.blurb: Sky-sailor and duelist, at home on rigging and rooftops, always one daring move ahead of gravity.
callingMaterial.class.alchemist.blurb: Magic in bottles: formulae brewed ahead of time, hurled, drunk, or poured, with the occasional glorious accident.
callingMaterial.class.gadgeteer.blurb: A walking workshop of grapnels, smoke, and spring-loaded surprises, with a gadget for every predicament.
callingMaterial.class.aether_channeler.b: A living conduit for the aether that drives the age: lightning in the veins and storms on a short leash.
callingMaterial.class.steam_knight.blurb: Armored in a hissing boilerplate shell, part cavalier and part locomotive, they hold the line and then become it.
callingMaterial.subclass.artificer.alche: An artificer who works in tinctures and reagents, healing allies and corroding enemies with thrown concoctions.
callingMaterial.subclass.artificer.armor: An artificer who lives inside their own powered armor, built either to guard the line or to strike from the dark.
callingMaterial.subclass.artificer.artil: An artificer who builds a small arcane cannon and turns a fight into a siege.
callingMaterial.subclass.artificer.battl: An artificer who fights beside a construct companion and repairs the party as readily as their gear.
callingMaterial.subclass.barbarian.path_: A barbarian whose rage becomes a frenzy: an extra attack while raging, immunity to fear and charm, and a presence that cows enemies.
A barbarian who takes a beast as a spirit guide, borrowing its strengths in and out of a rage.
Ancestral spirits answer this barbarian's rage and shield the people fighting beside them.
Rage manifests as a 10-foot aura of desert heat, arctic cold, or sea storm.
A divine champion whose fury is holy, and who death itself has trouble keeping.
Rage grows weapons out of the barbarian's own body: claws, a tail, savage teeth.
Raw magic leaks out of this barbarian every time their temper does.
A barbarian who channels giantkind, growing to their size and hurling what comes to hand.
callingMaterial.subclass.bard.college_of: A bard who collects knowledge from every discipline, cutting enemies down with words and borrowing spells from any class list.
A battle-skald who fights in the front rank and turns the fight itself into the song.
Feywild-touched charm: this bard rescues allies with a word and commands rooms on presence alone.
A blade-dancing performer whose weapon flourishes are the performance.
A bard who trades in fear and secrets and wears other people's lives like costumes.
A rhetorician who never misses with a word and never wastes an inspiration die.
The Song of Creation still echoes, and this bard can sing objects and dancing things into being.
A medium who calls up stories from the dead and lets the tale decide what happens next.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.life_dom: A cleric of healing and vitality, whose cures restore more, whose armor is heavy, and whose domain spells are always prepared.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.knowledg: A cleric of the gods of learning, for whom every secret is a form of power.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.light_do: A cleric of sun and flame who burns away darkness and the things that hide in it.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.nature_d: A priest of the wild gods, as at home with beasts and weather as with prayer.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.tempest_: Thunder and lightning made doctrine: this cleric answers insult with a storm.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.trickery: A holy trickster whose blessings are disguises, duplicates and well-aimed mischief.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.war_doma: A battle priest whose god expects the front line, not the back rank.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.death_do: A cleric of the gods of endings, comfortable with necrotic power and the grave's authority.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.forge_do: A smith-priest who blesses armor and weapons and treats the anvil as an altar.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.grave_do: A warden of the border between life and death who hates undeath more than dying.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.order_do: A cleric of law and hierarchy who turns obedience into a battlefield asset.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.peace_do: A binder of bonds whose blessing makes a party fight and endure as one thing.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.twilight: A shepherd of the border hour, granting sight in the dark and calm against terror.
callingMaterial.subclass.cleric.arcana_d: A cleric of the gods of magic itself, as much a scholar of spellcraft as a priest.
callingMaterial.subclass.druid.circle_of: A druid attuned to one kind of terrain, with bonus spells drawn from it, an extra cantrip and slots recovered on a short rest.
A druid who fights as a beast, shifting fast and into far more dangerous shapes than most.
A druid tied to the Summer Court, offering rest, safe camps and moonlit escape routes.
A speaker for the spirits of beasts and fey who summons help and keeps it alive.
A druid of decay who sees rot as part of the cycle and wears a halo of necrotic spores.
A druid who reads the constellations and takes their shapes: archer, chalice and dragon.
A druid bonded to a wildfire spirit, holding to the truth that fire clears ground for new growth.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.champio: A fighter of raw physical prowess: critical hits on a 19, remarkable athletics and a second fighting style.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.battle_: A student of martial technique who spends superiority dice on precise, tide-turning maneuvers.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.eldritc: A fighter who braids wizard magic into swordplay, casting and striking in the same breath.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.arcane_: An elf-trained bowman who puts a spell on the arrow instead of in the air.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.cavalie: A mounted champion and battlefield anchor who makes enemies regret walking past.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.samurai: A relentless warrior whose sheer conviction keeps them upright long past the point of sense.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.echo_kn: A fighter haunted by a shard of another timeline, fighting beside a grey echo of themselves.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.psi_war: A soldier whose mind is the weapon: telekinetic shoves, force shields and psionic strikes.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.rune_kn: A warrior taught giant runecraft, carving power into gear and growing to giant size at need.
callingMaterial.subclass.fighter.bannere: A knight-commander whose presence steadies a whole unit and spreads their own resilience around.
callingMaterial.subclass.monk.way_of_the: A monk who masters unarmed combat, knocking foes down and away with every flurry and healing with ki.
callingMaterial.subclass.monk.way_of_sha: A ninja-monk who bends darkness, steps between shadows and strikes from nowhere.
callingMaterial.subclass.monk.way_of_the: A monk who shapes ki into raw elemental magic: fists of fire, gusts of wind, walls of stone.
A monk who fights like a stumbling drunk and is never where the blow lands.
A weapon-saint who treats a chosen blade or bow as an extension of their unarmed art.
A monk who burns ki as radiant light, striking at range and flaring like a small sun.
A monk who studies dying itself, drawing strength from every death nearby.
callingMaterial.subclass.monk.way_of_mer: A masked healer-assassin whose hands can close a wound or stop a heart with the same touch.
callingMaterial.subclass.monk.way_of_the: A monk who summons their own spirit outward as glowing arms, a watching visage and a full body.
A monk who studies dragons until their ki breathes, roars and flies like one.
callingMaterial.subclass.paladin.oath_of: A paladin sworn to honesty, courage and compassion, with a sacred weapon and protection from fiends and undead.
A paladin sworn to light and life rather than law, shielding what is good from despair.
A paladin who has chosen one wrong to punish and will spend everything to reach it.
A paladin who believes order is imposed, and rules the battlefield through fear.
A paladin who fights only when talking fails, and takes the blows meant for others.
A paladin who chases the heroic deed itself, and drags the whole party up to that standard.
A paladin trained to detect and destroy extraplanar intruders before they take root.
A paladin sworn to a realm and its law, holding the line so others can fall back.
callingMaterial.subclass.paladin.oathbre: A paladin who broke their oath for darker power and now commands the undead. Usually a villain.
callingMaterial.subclass.ranger.hunter.b: A ranger who studies prey and picks a fighting technique to bring down hordes or giants.
callingMaterial.subclass.ranger.beast_ma: A ranger who fights alongside a bonded animal companion that acts on their command.
callingMaterial.subclass.ranger.gloom_st: A ranger of the lightless places who is deadliest in the first seconds of a fight.
callingMaterial.subclass.ranger.horizon_: A ranger who patrols the seams between planes and steps through them mid-fight.
callingMaterial.subclass.ranger.monster_: A ranger trained on the things that hunt people: their tricks, their saves, their weaknesses.
callingMaterial.subclass.ranger.fey_wand: A ranger carrying a piece of the Feywild: a strange mien, cutting words and psychic strikes.
callingMaterial.subclass.ranger.swarmkee: A ranger accompanied by a bound swarm of tiny nature spirits that bite, shove and carry.
callingMaterial.subclass.ranger.drakewar: A ranger bonded to a young draconic spirit that grows from a helper into a mount.
callingMaterial.subclass.rogue.thief.blu: A rogue of quick hands and quick feet: faster climbing, items used as a bonus action, and stealth on the move.
A killer who opens fights already having won them, and wears other people's faces to get close.
callingMaterial.subclass.rogue.arcane_tr: A thief who studied just enough wizardry to make locks, pockets and minds easier work.
callingMaterial.subclass.rogue.mastermin: A schemer who reads people, plants words and directs the fight from behind an ally's shoulder.
callingMaterial.subclass.rogue.swashbuck: A duellist who fights in the open, one on one, and talks the whole time.
callingMaterial.subclass.rogue.inquisiti: A detective-rogue who finds the tell, the lie and the weak point, then puts a blade in it.
callingMaterial.subclass.rogue.scout.blu: A skirmisher and pathfinder who slips out of reach the moment anyone closes.
callingMaterial.subclass.rogue.phantom.b: A rogue standing half in the land of the dead, collecting skills and souls as they go.
callingMaterial.subclass.rogue.soulknife: A rogue whose weapons are made of thought, thrown and re-formed at will.
callingMaterial.subclass.sorcerer.dracon: A sorcerer whose magic comes from a dragon ancestor: tougher scales, an elemental affinity and, in time, wings.
callingMaterial.subclass.sorcerer.wild_m: A sorcerer whose power came from somewhere chaotic and has never fully settled down.
callingMaterial.subclass.sorcerer.divine: A sorcerer whose bloodline runs back to something divine, mixing cleric magic into raw sorcery.
callingMaterial.subclass.sorcerer.shadow: A sorcerer touched by the Shadowfell, hard to kill and accompanied by a hound of ill omen.
callingMaterial.subclass.sorcerer.storm_: A sorcerer of wind and thunder who drifts through fights on their own weather.
callingMaterial.subclass.sorcerer.aberra: A sorcerer whose gift came from something far outside, and speaks in telepathy and warped magic.
callingMaterial.subclass.sorcerer.clockw: A sorcerer aligned to the machinery of absolute order, smoothing chaos out of the world.
callingMaterial.subclass.sorcerer.lunar_: A sorcerer whose magic waxes and wanes with a moon phase they can choose at will.
callingMaterial.subclass.warlock.the_fie: A warlock whose patron is a fiend of the lower planes, granting fiery spells and temporary hit points on a kill.
callingMaterial.subclass.warlock.the_arc: A pact with a lord or lady of the Feywild: charm, illusion and very sharp bargains.
callingMaterial.subclass.warlock.the_gre: A pact with something vast and probably unaware of you, paid in telepathy and madness.
callingMaterial.subclass.warlock.the_cel: A pact with a being of the Upper Planes: radiant fire in one hand, healing light in the other.
callingMaterial.subclass.warlock.the_hex: A pact with a sentient weapon from the Shadowfell: a warlock who fights in armor, with a blade.
callingMaterial.subclass.warlock.the_fat: A pact with something in the deep water, which sends a tentacle when called.
callingMaterial.subclass.warlock.the_gen: A pact with a noble genie, carrying their element and a vessel you can climb inside.

callingMaterial.subclass.wizard.bladesin: An elven tradition of sword-dance and spell, trading a heavy spellbook for footwork.
callingMaterial.subclass.wizard.chronurg: A wizard of Wildemount who manipulates time itself: initiative, durations and dice.
callingMaterial.subclass.wizard.gravitur: A wizard of Wildemount who bends weight and gravity, crushing, slowing and hurling.

spellMaterial.support.1: The natural weapons (1d6, magic, +1 to attack and damage) and Aquatic Adaptation's swim speed and water breathing are the DM's to apply.
spellMaterial.support.2: The astral forms, the silver cord and the return to the bodies are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.3: The awakened creature's INT 10, its language and its 30 days charmed are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.4: The vessel, its 120 days to mature and the soul's move into it are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.5: The server rolls the DC 15 INT save and the 6d6 psychic; the five answers and how long the insanity lasts are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.6: The weather's stages, how they change over time and what they do are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.7: The WIS save to probe deeper and the INT check to end the probe are the DM's; the server keeps the concentration.
spellMaterial.support.8: Arriving in an occupied space (4d6 force each, and the spell fails) is the DM's; tokens are moved by hand.
spellMaterial.support.9: The WIS save against a hostile messenger, the 3d6 psychic and the lost rest are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.10: The 5d10 radiant or necrotic to the chosen creature types entering or starting a turn there is the DM's to deal.
spellMaterial.support.11: The server rolls the WIS save and keeps the charm for its days; the 5d10 psychic for acting against the command, once a day, is the DM's to deal.
spellMaterial.support.12: The trigger, the explosive rune's DEX save and 5d8, or the stored spell, are the DM's when the glyph goes off.
spellMaterial.support.13: The extra effect (courage, darkness, energy vulnerability and the rest) and the CHA save against it are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.14: A hostile creature holding or wearing the object makes a DEX save to avoid it; that save is the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.15: The CHA save to cross, the barrier and the disadvantage on attacks are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.16: The CHA save to possess, the host's statistics and the soul's return are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.17: Damage to the stone (6d6 bludgeoning when partly destroyed, 50 force and expulsion when destroyed) is the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.18: The CHA save and the bound creature's service are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.19: The illusion's movement, the Investigation check to see through it and sensing through it are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.20: The WIS save, its modifiers for knowledge and connection, and the sensor are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.21: The CHA save of an unwilling creature and the Investigation check to see through it are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.22: The copy (half the hit points, no slots regained, 100 gp per hit point to repair), its obedience and the one-at-a-time limit are the DM's; it joins as a companion by hand.
spellMaterial.support.23: The plants' answers, the terrain they move and their cooperation are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.24: The contested STR check against the caster's ability modifier and the moving of a creature or object are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.25: The familiarity table's d100, a mishap's 3d10 force and reroll, and an off-target or similar-area arrival are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.26: The 1d4 + 1 turns in a row, and the spell ending when an action affects another creature, are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.27: Duplicating a spell of 8th level or lower casts that spell; any other effect, and the stress (2d10 necrotic per spell until a long rest, STR 3 for 2d4 days, a 33 percent chance of never casting Wish again), are the DM's.
spellMaterial.support.28: The CHA save on entering or starting a turn there, and each creature's awareness of it, are the DM's.
spellMaterial.starter.bard: You know a small fixed list of spells and cast with Charisma. Pick a mix of one good damage option and several ways to control a scene.
spellMaterial.starter.cleric: You prepare spells fresh after each long rest from the whole cleric list, so you can adapt daily. Wisdom is your casting ability.
spellMaterial.starter.druid: You prepare spells fresh after each long rest from the whole druid list. Wisdom is your casting ability, and you also have Wild Shape.
spellMaterial.starter.paladin: You prepare a small list from the paladin spells and cast with Charisma. Most of your damage still comes from your weapon and Divine Smite.
spellMaterial.starter.ranger: You know a small fixed list and cast with Wisdom. Your spells mostly sharpen your weapon attacks and your travel.
spellMaterial.starter.sorcerer: You know a very small fixed list, so pick versatile spells. Charisma is your casting ability, and Metamagic bends what you cast.
spellMaterial.starter.warlock: You have very few slots but they come back on a short rest and always cast at their highest level. Charisma is your casting ability.
spellMaterial.starter.wizard: You have the largest spell list in the game and prepare fresh each day from your spellbook. Intelligence is your casting ability.
spellMaterial.starter.artificer: You prepare a small list and cast with Intelligence, using your tools as a focus. Your infusions matter as much as your spells.

builderPicker.alignmentInfo: Alignment is a two-word shorthand for how your character treats rules (lawful, neutral, chaotic) and other people (good, neutral, evil). It binds nothing: it is a note to yourself and to the DM about how this person tends to act, and characters drift over a campaign. Pick the one that sounds most like them and stop worrying about it.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.LG: Does the right thing, by the rules. Keeps promises, protects the weak, trusts institutions to be worth defending. The paladin's default.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.NG: Does the most good available, law or no law. Helps whoever is in front of them without much regard for who is owed what.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.CG: Does the right thing, and breaks whatever rule is in the way. Rebels, smugglers with a conscience, people who free prisoners first and ask later.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.LN: Order for its own sake. The judge, the soldier, the monk: the code matters more than any one outcome it produces.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.N: No strong pull either way. Gets on with life, takes a side when a side has to be taken. The commonest alignment for ordinary people.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.CN: Freedom above all, their own most of all. Unpredictable but not cruel. Easy to play badly; check with your table before choosing it.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.LE: Takes what they want, within a system they respect and use. Tyrants, corrupt officials, devils. Keeps their word, which makes them worse.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.NE: Takes what they want and feels no need to dress it up. Loyal to nobody but themselves.
builderPicker.alignmentBlurb.CE: Destruction for its own sake. Almost always an NPC alignment; a party rarely survives one.
